mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth indicates strong economic activity, leading to increased corporate earnings and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative despite positive GDP growth over a 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and increasing S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when unemployment is below 3.5% in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production and housing starts indicate strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when both INDPRO and HOUST increase in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate above 4.5% during a tightening cycle may lead to decreased borrowing and lower S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales indicate strong consumer spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative despite rising RSAFS in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment suggests economic growth, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when PAYEMS increases in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high CPI and low FEDFUNDS may indicate inflationary pressures, leading to lower S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS decreases in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production indicates weaker supply chains, leading to lower S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when INDPRO decreases in more than 40% of cases.
